schemasAdded.title: sapphirus.foundry-deployment.v1
schemasAdded.role: Describes what physically exists in the Foundry project.

schemasAdded.title: sapphirus.model-profile.v1
schemasAdded.role: Describes what the organization permits and how Forge uses it. This is the only contract in which a deployment name legitimately appears, and it is never projected to the desktop.
schemasAdded.stableIdentity: profileId is organization-chosen and deliberately independent of deploymentName, so a deployment can be replaced without invalidating a persisted user selection.

schemasAdded.title: sapphirus.model-catalog.v1
schemasAdded.role: The sanitized effective catalog projected to the desktop: the intersection of deployment inventory, enabled signed profiles, policy, qualification, and subject/device entitlement.

availabilityVocabulary.design: The seven availability states the task names are split across two reachable enums rather than one loose seven-state enum. A selectable projection is structurally incapable of carrying a blocked state, so a profile that should not have been listed cannot describe itself as blocked.
availabilityVocabulary.blockedProfilesAreStillNamed: Visible but non-invocable profiles appear in unavailableProfiles carrying only profileId, displayName, the blocked state, and a recovery action. This is what lets the desktop explain why a previously selected profile disappeared instead of silently switching models, which FND-041 and FND-051 both require. No group name, deployment name, endpoint, or role assignment is representable there.

invalid.proves: A deployment name cannot be serialized into a desktop profile projection.
The Foundry project endpoint cannot be serialized into the desktop catalog.
A managed-identity client ID and a subscription ID cannot be serialized into the desktop catalog.
A selectable profile projection cannot carry a blocked availability state.
A profile without qualification evidence fails closed.
A raw provider capability key cannot survive into the canonical deployment contract; only the allowlisted canonical names exist.

registrationSurfaces.note: A new schema family must be added to nine hand-maintained lists in this repository. Two of them fail before generation with opaque codes and are recorded here so later contract tasks do not rediscover them.
lists: packages/contracts/scripts/lib/native-codegen.mjs productionRoots constant, cross-checked against the tool lock
packages/contracts/scripts/generate.mjs fixture literals and the fixture catalog tuple array

observedFailures.cause: The productionRoots constant in native-codegen.mjs was not updated alongside tool-lock.json. Generation refuses before running.
observedFailures.resolution: Both lists must name the family.

observedFailures.code: Generated TypeScript must not use any
observedFailures.cause: check-generated-bindings.mjs regexes /\bany\b/ across the whole generated text including doc comments. A schema description reading 'independent of any Foundry deployment name' failed the gate.
observedFailures.resolution: Schema descriptions must avoid the bare word in lowercase. The check is blunt but it also guarantees no generated any can hide inside a description.

generation.determinism: Both generators ran twice into separate clean staging roots and were compared byte-for-byte before any committed output was touched.

constraintsObserved: productionOptionalNullablePolicy is fail-closed-v1: a production property may not be both optional and nullable. Every nullable field in these three schemas is required-and-nullable.

The TypeScript generator runs with unreachableDefinitions:false, so a $def no root reaches produces no type in any language. The blocked-availability vocabulary is reachable through unavailableProfiles for exactly this reason.
